html:
In 529 the emperor Justinian barred pagans from teaching, and the school of Neoplatonist philosophy at Athens came to an end. The date is often used to mark the end of ancient philosophy and the classical world.

The school saw itself as the heir of Plato's Academy, revived around 410. Its last head was Damascius. After the ban he and six other philosophers, among them Simplicius, went to Persia around 531 to the court of Khosrow I, who had a name as a lover of learning. They were disappointed and came back. The Perpetual Peace of 532 included a clause letting them live by their own beliefs without harm.

Historians argue about how sudden the end was. Simplicius went on writing commentaries on Aristotle, and Platonic teaching continued in Alexandria under Christian teachers.
sum: In 529 the emperor Justinian barred pagans from teaching, and the school of Neoplatonist philosophy at Athens came to an end. The date is often used to mark the end of ancient philosophy and the classical world.
